To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Eustachian Tube Obstruction (ETO) test was able to differentiate patients with allergic rhinititis (AR) from patients without AR.

1) Eustachian Tube Obstruction (ETO) developed more frequently in patients with AR than in patients without AR after a dose of 0.1-0.5 mg of histamine; and 2) Saline challenges provoked a similar degree of ETO in patients with and without AR, suggesting that a hyperresponsiveness to histamine was responsible for the difference in ETO between patients with and without allergic rhinitis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pathogenesis of otitis media with fluid (OME) with the goal of improving our understanding of this common problem.
the role of Eustachian tubal function in the pathogenesis of otitis media with fluid.

the role of the Eustachian (auditory) tube in the development of otitis media with fluid in the middle ear, and the possible relationship of allergic rhinitis and other nasal diseases to otitis media.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
histamine nasal challenge is not a good test for the diagnosis of AR.
the Eustachian Tube Obstruction (ETO) is a result of allergic rhinitis and not the other way around.
ETO is not a common finding in subjects with AR and is not a common sequela to histamine nasal provocations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Eustachian Tube Obstruction is a very important factor in the development of otitis media with fluid.
histamine provocation is a useful test to assess the Eustachian tubal response in subjects with allergic disease.

histamine provocation can be used as an objective measure to assess the nasal mucosal responsiveness of subjects with AR, but the results of this study suggest that the nasal mucosa of subjects with AR is not the sole site of hyperresponsiveness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a new model for Eustachian Tube Obstruction that can be used to study Eustachian Tubal dysfunction in patients with otitis media and in patients with allergic rhinititis.
the Eustachian tubes are very responsive and can become easily obstructed.
the Eustachian Tube Obstruction Test (ETOT) may be used to differentiate between subjects with allergic rhinosinusitis (AR) and subjects without AR.
